messages.content: 你能幫我找到加州洛杉磯的素食餐廳嗎？它們至少要營業到晚上10點，然後也幫我找一下加州舊金山和華盛頓州西雅圖的素食餐廳嗎？

function.name: vegan_restaurant_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby vegan restaurants based on specific criteria like operating hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. New York, NY

operating_hours.description: Preferred latest closing time of the restaurant. E.g. if 11 is given, then restaurants that close at or after 11 PM will be considered. This is in 24 hour format.

message.reasoning:
The user wants vegan restaurants in Los Angeles (California) that stay open until at least 10pm. Also wants vegan restaurants in San Francisco (California) and Seattle (Washington). They didn't specify operating hours for SF and Seattle; maybe we can use default 21? But they might want all vegan restaurants regardless of hours. The function signature includes location and optional operating_hours. For LA we need operating_hours=22. For SF and Seattle we can just call with location only.

We should call the function twice: one for LA with operating_hours=22, one for SF and Seattle combined? The function expects a single location string. We could call separately for each city. So two calls: one for "Los Angeles, CA" with operating_hours=22, one for "San Francisco, CA" without specifying operating_hours (default 21). And also one for "Seattle, WA". That would be three calls. But the user asked for LA, SF, and Seattle. We can combine SF and Seattle into separate calls. So total three calls.

We need to output the function calls. According to guidelines, we should not provide additional text besides the function calls. So we produce JSON calls. We'll do them sequentially.
